title: Load balancing and proxies
summary: What a load balancer does, common algorithms, L4 vs L7, health checks, sticky sessions, and the difference between a forward and a reverse proxy.
note:
1. Load balancer = one entry point spreading traffic over many servers
2. Algorithms: round-robin, least-connections, weighted, IP/consistent hash
3. L4 (TCP, fast, blind) vs L7 (HTTP, routes on path/header, TLS)
4. Health checks drop dead nodes; sticky sessions pin a user (avoid if stateless)
5. Reverse proxy (in front of servers) vs forward proxy (in front of clients)
✎ In my words: ______________________________________________

recall.a: L4 routes on TCP/IP (fast, content-blind); L7 routes on HTTP data like path/headers and can terminate TLS.
They pin a user to one server, breaking stateless scaling and reducing fault tolerance; keep state shared instead.
Reverse proxy sits in front of servers (clients see it); forward proxy sits in front of clients (servers see it).

shot.title: LB algorithms
shot.body:
| algorithm | picks server by | good for |
|---|---|---|
| round-robin | next in rotation | uniform requests |
| least-connections | fewest active conns | uneven request cost |
| weighted | capacity weight | mixed hardware |
| IP/consistent hash | hash(key) | cache affinity, sharding |

sections.title: What a load balancer does
sections.body:
✍️ A load balancer is the single public entry point that spreads incoming requests across a pool of servers, so no one box is overwhelmed and failed boxes are routed around.
✍️ It also enables rolling deploys (drain a node, update, return it) and can terminate TLS centrally.

sections.title: Balancing algorithms
sections.body: ✍️ **Round-robin:** next server in order — simple, assumes equal requests. **Least-connections:** send to the server with fewest active connections — better when request cost varies. **Weighted:** bias toward beefier machines. **Consistent/IP hash:** `hash(key) → server`, keeping a given key on the same node (cache affinity, sharding).

sections.title: L4 vs L7
Health checks and sticky sessions
sections.body:
✍️ **Health checks:** the LB periodically pings a `/health` endpoint and removes nodes that fail, so traffic only goes to live servers.
- **Sticky sessions** pin a client to one server via a cookie. They let you keep in-memory session state but break clean horizontal scaling and hurt failover — prefer a stateless design with shared session storage.

sections.title: Reverse vs forward proxy
sections.body: ✍️ A **reverse proxy** sits in front of your servers and faces clients (a load balancer, CDN edge, or NGINX doing TLS/caching). A **forward proxy** sits in front of clients and faces the internet (corporate egress, content filtering). A load balancer is a specialized reverse proxy.
